question.problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the parabolic cylinders $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=16-{z}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-4}^{4}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,z)\,dz\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xz$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =16-{z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =16\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xz$-plane is a circle.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type III region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 16-{z}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the circle ${x}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{16-{z}^{2}}\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(16-{z}^{2})-({x}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}},$

for $-4\le x\le 4.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}{\int }_{-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}}}\,16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f(y,z) & ={(-\sqrt{16-{x}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{16-{z}^{2}})}^{2}+(16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =(16-{x}^{2})+(16-{x}^{2})+(16-{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =48-3{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
